patch.objective: Screen for depression and anxiety, assess suicide risk, and start treatment or refer
secondaryObjectives: Assess genetic, behavioral, sexual, lifestyle, cultural and social risk

sources.cite: Family nurse practitioner test content outline (effective 2026-10-30), IV. Implementation (33%)
sources.note: Relayed from the course seed (backend/supabase/seed/tracks/fnp.ts), which read it 2026-11-14; the objective title is the course's own.

sources.cite: The Columbia Lighthouse Project, Columbia Protocol (C-SSRS) triage page: 'the most worrisome answers are a recent (past month) yes to items 4 or 5' (intent, intent with a plan) 'and/or any recent (3 months) behavior'; next steps 'are setting specific', and 'interventions should be changed to reflect your individual resources and policies'
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 (summarizing fetch with quotes; page last modified 2024-03-22). The screener's items, relayed from the NCMHCE session (read 2026-11-11): wish to be dead; suicidal thoughts; thoughts with method; intent without plan; intent with plan; suicidal behavior.

sources.cite: Stanley B, Brown GK, et al. Comparison of the Safety Planning Intervention with follow-up vs usual care of suicidal patients treated in the emergency department. JAMA Psychiatry 2018;75(9):894-900 (SPRC summary): six steps, the last making the environment safer through lethal means counseling; with phone follow-up within 72 hours of discharge, about half as likely to engage in suicidal behavior over six months
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 on SPRC's summary page (summarizing fetch). The original six steps were also read for the EPPP sessions on 2026-11-10 (Stanley and Brown 2012, which presents the plan as an alternative to no-suicide contracts).

sources.cite: SAMHSA, SAFE-T: Suicide Assessment Five-Step Evaluation and Triage (PEP24-01-036): identify risk and protective factors, conduct a suicide inquiry, determine the risk level and interventions, and document a treatment plan
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 on SAMHSA's product page (summarizing fetch). The page names the activities without the card's risk-level table, which was not read.

sources.cite: The Joint Commission, R3 Report Issue 18: National Patient Safety Goal for suicide prevention, NPSG.15.01.01 (effective 2019-07-01): EP1 environmental risk assessment; EP2 screen 'using a validated screening tool'; EP3 an assessment that 'directly asks about suicidal ideation, plan, intent, suicidal or self-harm behaviors'; EP4 document the risk level and the mitigation plan; EP5-EP7 policies for monitoring, discharge counseling and follow-up
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 (summarizing fetch with quotes; issue dated 2019-11-20, updated 2025-12-03). The report names one-to-one monitoring as a key protocol on nonpsychiatric units; it does not itself require it, so the observation level in each sim is the facility's policy.

sources.cite: Suicide Prevention Resource Center (SAMHSA-funded), Support safe care transitions and create organizational linkages: 'Make a follow-up appointment for the patient before discharge', ideally within 48 hours; 'Involve family, friends, and other loved ones'; follow-up contacts by phone, text or email; 'Transmit patient health information to referral providers'
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 (summarizing fetch with quotes, first 100,000 characters of the page).

sources.cite: SAMHSA, 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline: 'Call or Text 988'
sources.note: Relayed from the EPPP sessions (read 2026-11-10), not re-read here.
